info.name: Shop & Product APIs
info.description:
Combined test kit: SHOPS (CRUD with multiple_images/rating/likes, teams, members, editor) + PRODUCTS (pricing types, variations, likes, per-user ratings 0-10, views, tags, trust flags, admin badges, media files, manual discount codes with usage limits, automatic quantity rules, single-discount price preview).

ORDER: 1) Login (user). 2) Create shop — shopId auto-saves. 3) Create product — productId + variationId auto-save. 4) Everything else chains from saved variables.

PERMISSIONS: shop creator owns everything shop/product-side; shop editor can edit shop fields only; admin only touches product/service badges — never shop teams.

request.description:
IMAGES ARE UPLOADED HERE — the client no longer calls POST /file/short first. Attach the picked file(s) directly and the server pushes them to S3 and generates a thumbnail for each (same pipeline as /file/short). Response returns header_image + header_image_thumbnail, profile_image + profile_image_thumbnail, and images[] with { url, thumbnailUrl }.

Fields: header_image (1 file), profile_image (1 file), multiple_images (up to 10 files — select several in the one row).
Accepted: jpg, jpeg, png, webp, gif, bmp, tiff. Max 25MB per image.

BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: any of the three may instead be sent as a plain URL string (as the disabled text rows show), which is stored as-is with thumbnail = null. Files and URLs may be mixed in multiple_images.

In a multipart body, arrays go as JSON strings — teams: [1,2], members: [3].

item.name: 6. Product Cart
item.description:
Buyer-facing product cart — one implicit cart per user (no separate cart container, no cart selection step). Separate from the SERVICE cart (folder not shown here) and from the legacy /addToCart endpoint — this is the new /product-cart module.

RULES:
- Non-variation products (hasVariations:false): send only shopProductId. variationId must be omitted.

item.name: 7. Product Orders
item.description:
Cart → order checkout, wallet-based payment, order status lifecycle, and post-order shipping/transport charges.

STRUCTURE: checkout creates ONE parent order (e.g. #PO-...-FLG4LI, one wallet debit for the whole cart) which fans out into one SHOP-ORDER per shop represented in the cart (e.g. #PO-...-FLG4LI-1, #PO-...-FLG4LI-2 — one per shop, each independently paid out and independently tracked). The buyer's order list shows parent orders (with shop-orders nested inside); a shop owner's order list shows only THEIR shop's shop-orders.

WALLET: checkout takes a walletId (not walletType+currency) — the wallet row itself already encodes both, so there's no ambiguity when a buyer holds multiple wallets of the same type in different currencies. If a shop's payout wallet currency doesn't match the buyer's chosen wallet currency, checkout is rejected before any money moves (no FX conversion in this version).

STATUS: confirmed → processing → shipped → in_transit → customs → out_for_delivery → delivered, forward-only, shop-owner-or-admin only. cancelled / refunded / returned are side-branches reachable from any non-terminal state — setting one AUTOMATICALLY refunds whatever the buyer paid on that shop-order back to their wallet and restores product/variation stock, in one transaction.

CHARGES: shop owner (or admin) can add a post-order charge (e.g. "International shipping — $15") to a shop-order — this only raises the shop-order's totalAmount (a balance becomes due), no money moves yet. The buyer then explicitly pays it via a separate call, choosing any wallet of theirs at that moment (may differ from the checkout wallet).

ORDER TO RUN: 1) Login as buyer. 2) Add items to cart (folder 6). 3) Checkout — parentOrderId/shopOrderId auto-save. 4) Login as the shop owner (separate token) to update status / add a charge. 5) Back to buyer token to pay a charge.

item.name: 9. Product Add-ons
item.description:
Seller-facing CRUD for product add-ons — optional extras a buyer can attach when adding a product/variation to cart (e.g. "Extra battery — $15"). Images are uploaded from the client as multipart files (like product/variation images) — NOT a URL string field — each gets pushed to S3 with a generated thumbnail.

SCOPING IS MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, same rule as pricing/stock: a non-variation product (hasVariations:false) owns its add-ons directly (POST /:productId/add-ons); a variation product (hasVariations:true) owns add-ons per-variation instead (POST /:productId/variations/:variationId/add-ons). Creating a product-level add-on on a variation product (or vice versa) returns 422.

Add-on selection when adding to cart is on/off only (no per-add-on quantity) — see folder "6. Product Cart" for the buyer-facing add/remove-from-cart-line endpoints. The cart snapshot only carries the FIRST image as a single URL, not the whole gallery.
